## Added

- New `dossier` command: assembles the whole-dossier annotation — per-page
  labels, text-extraction routing, decoded QR payloads, entities, groups and a
  derived document graph, with the `vector` classification and georeferencing
  folded in. Pages deterministic extraction cannot read (scans, handwriting,
  mis-encoded text layers) carry an `extraction.vlm` work order; a second run
  with `--answers <file>` merges the vision pass's results. With `--output`,
  each drawing page's GeoJSON is written under `geojson/<document>/` and
  referenced from `pages[].cad.geojson`.
- `docs/annotation-schema.md`: the annotation's field reference (schema
  version 0.2.0) and the `--answers` file format. `docs/json-api.md` gained
  the matching `dossier` contract section.
- QR decoding (pure Rust, `rxing`): two-tier — a 1400 px pass over every
  page, and a 3000 px retry for scans and e-cadastre-templated pages.
- Mis-encoded text-layer detection: legacy 8-bit (ArmSCII-style) and
  custom-glyph font mappings are flagged as `extraction.encoding_issue` and
  VLM-routed instead of being emitted as confident mojibake.
- `dossier --vlm [model]`: the vision pass can run in-process against a
  hosted model. Bare `--vlm` uses `gemini-3.8-flash`, the corpus benchmark's
  winner — `gemini-*` specs via the Gemini API (`GEMINI_API_KEY`),
  `vendor/model` specs via OpenRouter (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`), `gpt-*` specs
  via OpenAI (`OPENAI_API_KEY`). Networked and opt-in per invocation; it
  sends the flagged pages' images to the configured provider. Pages covered by
  `--answers` are not re-asked. Model comparison on the corpus task is in
  `docs/annotation-findings.md`.

- New experimental `cadfix` command: a hosted model proposes CAD fixes for
  one page — semantic layers, noise removal, ring closing — through parallel
  tool calls against an inventory of the extracted features; the operations
  are applied deterministically and the geometry never comes from the model.
- New experimental `building` command: reconstructs what the permit says
  the finished site must look like, from the drawing set's visualization
  section (development scheme, facades with level marks, roof plan,
  indicator table, 3D renders). One `add_part` tool call per structure —
  each house block of a development, the perimeter fence as a wall ring,
  pitched roofs as stepped insets, facade colours off the renders — plus a
  `facts` block with the printed indicator numbers. Footprints are exact
  extracted rings from the anchor sheet, georeferenced where it was placed;
  a printed sheet scale converts page-unit anchors to metres. When a floor
  plan draws the part's exact exterior outline, the model names that sheet
  (`parts[].outline_page`) and the toolkit extrudes the exact drawn
  outline — stitched from loose CAD polylines where needed, scaled by the
  sheet's printed scale, rigidly aligned onto the site position, and
  guarded by area and alignment residual. Output is map-native extruded
  GeoJSON (`height`/`base`/`color`). `--answers` labels sharpen sheet
  selection.
- Both new commands default to `--model gemini-3.8-flash`, like `--vlm`;
  `--model gpt-6-astra` (OpenAI, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, via the Responses API)
  is the higher-priced alternative, and `--vlm` now also takes `gpt-*`
  specs. Gemini function calling is wired, so every hosted surface works
  on every provider. Networked surfaces are now `--vlm`, `cadfix`, `building` —
  each still opt-in per invocation.
- New `llm-providers` crate: one transport over Gemini / OpenAI /
  OpenRouter with vision input, reasoning effort, and parallel tool calls.
  `.env.sample` at the repo root names every key. Every hosted call logs
  its token usage and estimated cost to stderr, priced from the bundled
  `models.json` catalog (rates recorded with source and date); overload
  and throttling responses get one bounded retry.

- Document-level placement propagation: sheets that print no coordinate
  table of their own — general plans, cadastral extracts, situation maps —
  are georeferenced by matching their drawn parcel outline against a
  confidently placed sibling sheet's table (`georeference.source` gains the
  value **`document_table`**). Guarded by the standard RANSAC consensus
  plus a borrowed-fit evidence gate (five-plus matched corners, or a
  complete small parcel at confident residual); on the private corpus this
  turns 9 placed pages into 30 with zero regressions. `printed_dimensions`
  never appears with a lent table.

- `dossier` gains a document-level **`request`** block: what the Ձև N 1-1
  application form asks for, read deterministically off the form's fixed
  slots — `action` from the form's own closed list (`new_construction`,
  `reconstruction`, `restoration`, `strengthening`, `change_of_use`,
  `other`), the `object` description, `use` (`residential` \| `commercial`
  \| `industrial` \| `mixed`, with `use_page` naming the page that said so;
  absent when no page does), secondary `works` (`demolition`, `annex`,
  `fence`, `basement`, …), `storeys`, the site `address` without its
  cadastral code, and the `planned` parameters line verbatim. Absent when
  no embedded-text application form states a request. On the ten dossiers
  of the corpus that carry the authority's reply, the action and use agree
  with the reply in every case.
- **Every placed page's GeoJSON now ends with the subject parcel**: a
  `Polygon` feature tagged `kind: "survey_parcel"`, built from the
  turning-point table the fit was made on (`area_m2`, `perimeter_m`,
  `turning_points`, `verified: true`). Counted in `summary.features` and
  `summary.polygons`. A caller draws or measures the boundary from this
  feature instead of guessing which drawn ring it is.
- `building` gains deterministic **site measurements**: a second
  FeatureCollection (`measurements`, and `building/<document>.measurements.geojson`
  under `--output`) holding the parcel polygon, every parcel and footprint
  side length, each building's setback to every parcel side, and
  building-to-building / building-to-fence clearances — each as the
  two-point `LineString` it was measured along, with `length_m` and a
  `label`. A `parcel` block names the ring used (`survey_parcel` on a
  placed anchor, else the declared `fence`, else the largest
  `enclosing_ring`) with its area and perimeter. Omitted, with a warning,
  when the frame is not metric or no parcel ring can be identified.
- `dossier`: a page that placed carries its `cad` block (and, unanswered,
  the label `cad_drawing`) even where the structural classifier called it
  `unknown` — a sheet fitted to the survey is a drawing by proof, and its
  georeferenced export is the one thing a caller cannot get elsewhere.
- **`--parcel <file>`** on `vector`, `dossier` and `building`: a GeoJSON
  file of WGS 84 parcel polygon(s) — the cadastre's own statement of the
  boundary — matched by shape to sheets that draw the parcel but print no
  coordinate table (`georeference.source: "parcel_polygon"`; the polygon
  appears in the page's collection as `kind: "reference_parcel"`). A
  stricter gate than a lent sibling table: two thirds of the corners at
  ≤ 0.1 m. On the corpus's dossier 1, which prints no table anywhere, the
  cadastre polygon places its five plan sheets with all fifteen corners at
  millimetre residual and puts the reconstructed houses on the map
  (`parcel.source: "reference_parcel"`).
- `dossier --vlm -o dir` writes the merged vision-pass answers as
  `answers/<document>.json` (`answers_file`), the file `building --answers`
  takes — one vision pass serves both commands.
- `building` anchors on the best placed sheet rather than the first in
  document order: drawn at 1:1000 or finer (a 1:2000 situation map never
  carries the design), holding the most structure-sized outlines, with a
  plan-view label (over a floor plan, whose rings are rooms) and then
  confidence of fit as tie-breaks, the parcel boundary itself never
  counting; a placed sheet with no building outline at all yields to an
  unplaced plan sheet that has some. The model's reasoning budget was raised
  (12k → 48k output tokens): on Gemini the thinking counts against it, and
  at 12k the reply was cut off mid-thought on half the corpus and read as
  "the model proposed no structure". A footprint candidate that is the
  parcel boundary — the survey or reference parcel, or a ring of the same
  size on the same spot — is named as such to the model and refused as a
  building (`warnings`: "candidate N is the parcel boundary"); a fence may
  still follow it. On three corpus dossiers the model had put the house on
  the parcel. Footprint candidates now include outlines that
  a CAD export drew as loose polylines, stitched into rings the same
  conservative way the exact-outline pass does — a survey sheet whose
  house is four separate wall segments no longer offers no candidate.

- Annotation semantics fixes (schema stays 0.2.0; the reviewed corpus
  annotations were regenerated): `sources[].via` now mirrors how a value
  was actually read (a legacy-encoded page's regex-read identifiers say
  `embedded_text`, not `vlm`); a live `--vlm` run routes pure-imagery
  pages `none` exactly like the same answer replayed from a file; an
  answer that names no groups gets the deterministic group derivation and
  certificate chaining instead of silently losing both; person/org ids
  sort their two name words, so the certificate's given-surname order and
  the passport's surname-given order land on one entity.

## Fixed

- **Placed geometry was 105 m off the Yerevan cadastre.** The Gauss-Krüger
  turning-point tables were run through the EPSG Pulkovo 1942 → WGS 84
  Helmert shift; the city's own cadastre (gis.yerevan.am) publishes the
  same parcels with the Krassovsky Transverse Mercator inverse taken as
  WGS 84 directly, and only that reading lands the survey on the city's
  parcel — 0.00 m centroid agreement on two corpus parcels, 105.6 m east /
  12.3 m north with the shift. The shift is gone; every placed page's
  coordinates and `georeference.center` move accordingly, with the
  residuals (`rmse_m`, fits in the projected frame) unchanged.

## Changed

- Contract version is now **0.9.0**. Existing command outputs are unchanged;
  the release is additive.
- API keys travel in request headers (Gemini: `x-goog-api-key`), never in
  URLs, so they cannot leak through a proxy log or a malformed-URL error;
  provider error bodies are surfaced in failures (Gemini's quota message
  instead of a bare `429`).
- Toolchain and dependencies moved to latest stable: Rust 1.98
  (`rust-version = "1.98"`), `clap` 4.6, `lopdf` 0.45, `pdfium-render` 0.9.4,
  and refreshed transitive locks. The corpus suite passes unchanged on the
  updated stack.
